Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to transfer their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Details below.

iOS will make app replacement easier

Although it doesn't happen often, developers sometimes retire an existing app and launch a new one to replace it, requiring users to switch to a separate standalone app.

Even though most developers strive to make the transition as smooth as possible, users still need to take some steps, especially when the data isn't stored in the cloud.

With the release of iOS 27.2, Apple will address this problem through a new system-managed migration flow that transfers the relevant data and supported settings to the designated replacement app before deleting the old app.

Based on the existing code in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following prompt:

"The developer of "%1$@" suggests transferring your existing app data and settings to a new app, "%2$@". Your iPhone can handle this for you before you start using the new app. Once finished, the old app will be removed from this iPhone."

Users can then choose to "Transfer App Data & Settings" or "Don't Transfer Anything." If users decline the migration, the system will show a second confirmation prompt warning that some preferences (including notification and location settings) may need to be reconfigured.

It's worth noting that this feature appears to be limited to cases where a developer replaces their own existing app with a designated successor app, and is not intended for transferring data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a number of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, location, and Health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus mode settings
  • App Lock and protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and Live Activities for accessories
  • Access permissions for related accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll be keeping a close eye on changes to this framework during the iOS 27.2 beta testing period, and will report further as we learn more about how developers implement this feature.
